message.content:
Adversarially review the geolocation pipeline of Earwitness, a video/photo forensics suite (FastAPI backend, repo at /Users/relesto/Downloads/earwitness, read CLAUDE.md first for conventions). Its findings are shown to non-expert hackathon judges, so honesty matters: the product must never present a wrong place with confidence, and must never crash a case.

Files to review (all of them, in full):
- src/earwitness/modules/geo.py — the module: proposes candidate places with an OpenAI model, gathers references, verifies with a second model pass, then applies deterministic rules (verified / vetoed / pinned by terrain) and emits findings, artifacts, and a published dict used by modules/weather.py and modules/brief.py.
- src/earwitness/terrain.py — skyline tracing (dynamic programming), elevation tiles (AWS terrarium), horizon rendering, grid search, chance control (mirrored/inverted skyline), judge().
- src/earwitness/georefs.py — OpenStreetMap Overpass feature counts and conflict logic; Mapillary + Wikimedia Commons street-level photos.
- tests/test_terrain.py, and the consumers: src/earwitness/modules/brief.py (search for "geo"), src/earwitness/modules/weather.py, web/src/components/viz/MapView.tsx, web/src/components/case/Sections.tsx (mapPoints/MapSection), web/src/lib/plain.ts (geo entries), docs/PROTOCOL.md.

Hunt for, in priority order:
1. Crashes / exceptions that escape the module (modules must only raise Skip; anything else marks it as error and loses the result): KeyErrors on model output, empty lists, None handling, numpy edge cases (all-NaN, empty arrays), division by zero, cv2 errors, httpx errors not caught, TimeoutError handling, asyncio misuse, file paths.
2. Logic errors in the decision rules: cases where a candidate gets "verified"/"Located" or pinned to terrain coordinates when it should not, or wrong index bookkeeping (candidate indices vs verdict indices vs shuffled order), wrong units (km vs m, degrees vs radians), sign errors in pitch/heading, wrap-around at 0/360 degrees, lat/lon swaps.
3. Geometry/maths bugs in terrain.py: projection consistency between _angles, render_horizon, draw_overlay; the Web Mercator tile maths in load_dem; DEM sampling (row/col orientation); detrend matrix; the null/control comparison fairness; anything that can make a false "strong" match more likely.
4. Overpass query correctness (QL syntax, quoting, around filter, count parsing order), Commons/Mapillary parsing, rate limits, and whether "conflicts" can be produced by API failures (a failure must never look like "feature absent").
5. Contract breaks with consumers: finding titles brief.py matches on, data keys the UI turns into map pins (data.latitude/longitude), JSON-ability of finding data, artifact kinds/ids vs plain.ts EXPLAIN prefixes.
6. Performance hazards on a 2-core VPS (CPU-bound work on the event loop instead of asyncio.to_thread, unbounded tile downloads, memory).

Rules: do not edit any files. You may run read-only commands and small Python snippets via `uv run python` from the repo root (e.g. to exercise a function with edge-case inputs), and `uv run pytest tests/test_terrain.py -q`. Do not call OpenAI (do not run the full module). Network calls to public APIs are fine in moderation.

Verify each finding before reporting it (point to the exact line, show the triggering input, and if cheap, reproduce it with a snippet). Report: a ranked list of confirmed defects (file:line, what goes wrong, concrete scenario, suggested fix), then a short list of plausible-but-unverified concerns, clearly separated. Skip style nits.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Earwitness is a video and photo forensics suite (HackTheBurgh 2026, G-Research "discover the invisible in data"): a FastAPI backend streams findings over a WebSocket to a React/Vite HUD. The demo is judged by non-experts, so every finding carries a plain-English `title`/`detail` that states its limits; nothing is hidden to simplify.

## Commands

```sh
uv sync                                   # Python 3.14; needs ffmpeg (>= 5.1) and tesseract on PATH
cp .env.example .env                      # TIMESCALE_SERVICE_URL is required; the server refuses to start without it
                                          # AUTH0_DOMAIN / AUTH0_CLIENT_ID / AUTH0_AUDIENCE enable writes (see Auth below)
uv run earwitness db migrate              # apply src/earwitness/schema.sql (idempotent; the server also does this)
uv run earwitness serve                   # http://127.0.0.1:8765, serves web/dist if built
uv run earwitness demo --out demo         # regenerate the demo pack (videos + demo/photos) and MANIFEST.json
(cd web && npm install && npm run dev)    # Vite dev server, proxies /api and /ws to :8765 (EARWITNESS_API overrides)
(cd web && npm run build)                 # tsc -b && vite build -> web/dist (committed build is what the server serves)

uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format src tests scripts
uv run pytest -q                          # ~2 min; needs the database (each run gets a throwaway schema seeded from the main grid record)
uv run pytest tests/test_photo.py -q      # still-image suite only (~40 s)
uv run pytest tests/test_auth.py -q       # Auth0 gate, tokens signed by a local RSA key (no network)
uv run pytest tests/test_modules.py -q -k "light"          # one test by keyword
uv run python scripts/evaluate.py OUT ~/Downloads/earwitness-tests/*   # real-clip regression: target 0 false edit alarms
bash scripts/deploy.sh                    # rsync + remote_setup.sh to the server (deploy key ~/.ssh/earwitness_deploy), restarts the systemd service
```

Tests set `EARWITNESS_OFFLINE=1` and pop `OPENAI_API_KEY`; note that `earwitness.db` calls `load_dotenv(.env)` at import, so pop the key *after* importing `earwitness.server.jobs` in ad-hoc scripts, or OpenAI modules will run.

## Architecture

**One case = one evidence file = one ordered run of modules.** `server/jobs.py:run_case` builds a `CaseContext` (`modules/base.py`), picks the module list from `modules/registry.py` by `ctx.kind` (`video` | `image`; audio-only uses the video set), emits a `case` event, then runs modules concurrently under a semaphore (`EARWITNESS_PARALLEL`, default 4). Every module is a class with `name`, `title`, `description`, optional `depends`, and `async run(ctx, out)`; it talks only through the `Reporter` (`out.progress/finding/artifact/log/path`). Modules must never raise past `Skip`; one failing module is recorded as `status: error` and the case continues.

**Cross-module data flows through `ctx.publish(name, value)` / `await ctx.wait_for(name)`**, keyed by module name. `run_case` publishes `None` for every module (of either kind) that is not scheduled, so `wait_for` on an absent module returns immediately instead of hanging 600 s. Dependencies listed in `depends` are awaited before the module starts; `depends = ["*"]` (brief) waits for everything.

**Events are the record.** `Case.emit` appends to `cases/<id>/events.jsonl` and fans out to WebSocket listeners; the UI (`web/src/lib/state.ts:reduce`) is a pure reducer over those events and replays them on reconnect. The DB (`db.py`, Tiger Data/TimescaleDB) is only an index (`cases`, `findings`) plus the shared GB grid-frequency record; a DB failure never sinks a case. Protocol and artifact kinds are documented in `docs/PROTOCOL.md` and mirrored in `web/src/lib/types.ts`; keep them in step when adding an event field or artifact kind.

**Decoded media is cached on the context:** `ctx.frames(width)`, `ctx.frame_at(t)`, `ctx.audio()` for video; `ctx.image()` (oriented full-res RGB), `ctx.image_scaled(w)` for stills. `frame_at` returns the still itself for images, which is how `ocr`, `vision` and `geo` serve both kinds with small `still = ctx.kind == "image"` branches. Shared photo parsing (EXIF with own TIFF walker, XMP, JPEG segments/quant tables, PNG chunks, quality estimate) lives in `photo.py`, not in modules.

**Module names double as UI keys.** The web layer maps module names to plain-language text, icons and tabs in `web/src/lib/plain.ts` (`MODULES`, `TABS`, `EXPLAIN` by artifact id prefix, `DATA_LABEL` for finding data keys). The image set reuses the names `provenance` and `tamper` (classes `PhotoProvenance`, `PhotoPixels`) so the existing UI mapping applies; new modules need entries there or they render as generic "additional check".

**Verdict and plain answers come from `modules/brief.py` alone**, by deterministic rules over finding tags/titles (`_local_brief` / `_plain_answers` for video, `_local_brief_photo` / `_photo_answers` for stills), with an optional OpenAI narrative and "dossier" labelled AI-inferred. Verdicts: `EDITED`, `POSSIBLY EDITED`, `NO SIGNS OF EDITING`, and for stills `AI-GENERATED` (`verdictOf` in plain.ts maps them). Tags are the contract: `splice`/`cut`/`clone` findings with warning+ severity drive EDITED; `editor`/`history`/`modified`/`resized` drive POSSIBLY; `declared`+`synthetic` drive AI-GENERATED. Findings matched by title prefix (e.g. "Taken on ", "ENF dates", "Embedded thumbnail") are also part of that contract: renaming a title can silently change the verdict or an answer.

**False-alarm discipline for pixel heuristics (stills).** ELA, grain, shifted-grid and per-block ghost regions are leads (`notice`, tags `ela`/`noise`/`grid`/`ghost`) and never move the verdict on their own; `photo_pixels.py` upgrades a lead to a `splice` warning only when a second independent trace overlaps the same `data.box`. Thumbnail mismatch, SIFT copy-move, appended data and declared generators are the trusted edit signals. Before changing any image detector, rerun it over the real unedited phone photos in `~/Downloads` (iPhone HEIC/JPEG, Samsung, WhatsApp/WeChat copies, screenshots) and the planted set from `demo_photo.py`; the standard is zero false "edited" verdicts on real originals.

**Auth (Auth0).** Viewing is open; every endpoint that changes evidence (`POST /api/cases`, `/from-path`, `/rerun`, `DELETE`) depends on `server/auth.py:require_user`, which verifies an RS256 access token for `AUTH0_AUDIENCE` issued by `AUTH0_DOMAIN` (JWKS fetched and cached). Without all three env vars those endpoints answer 503, never "open". `/api/health` publishes `auth` (domain, client id, audience: public values) and the SPA wraps itself in `Auth0Provider` only when it is present (`web/src/lib/auth.tsx`); `authHeaders()` in `lib/api.ts` attaches the bearer token and starts a login redirect when logged out, so any new write call must go through it. Enhance and the WebSocket stay unauthenticated. Module tests drive `CaseStore` directly and bypass HTTP, so they need no token; HTTP-level tests patch `auth._signing_key` as `tests/test_auth.py` does. The deployed server's `.env` holds the Auth0 values; `scripts/remote_setup.sh` does not write them.

**Stills in the UI.** `CaseInfo.kind === 'image'` swaps `Player` for `PhotoStage` (zoom/pan viewer, overlay maps = heatmap artifacts with `data.overlay: true`, boxes from findings' `data.box` as 0..1 fractions, lenses, magnifier, region enhance). `lib/region.ts` is the still-image counterpart of `lib/playback.ts`: a `useSyncExternalStore` store whose snapshot must stay referentially stable, plus `MediaKindContext` so shared widgets pick "photo"/"video" wording. `/api/cases/{id}/enhance` dispatches on kind: multi-frame super-resolution for video, full-res crop through forensic lenses for images.

## Conventions

- Finding `data` must be JSON-able (the Reporter rounds floats and converts numpy); keep heavy arrays out of it and write images/CSVs via `out.path(name)` + `out.artifact(..., file=path)`.
- Regions on stills are `data.box = {x, y, w, h}` fractions of the oriented picture (`photo.box_fraction`), never pixels of an analysis-size copy.
- Blocking numpy/OpenCV work goes through `asyncio.to_thread` so the event stream stays live.
- Python style: ruff (`E,F,W,I`, isort single-line), long human-readable strings may use `# fmt: skip`. Pattern-match `try/except A, B:` (3.14 syntax) is used throughout.
- Synthetic test media come from `demo.py` (video) and `demo_photo.py` (photos, planted truth in `PLANTED`); `synth.py` builds the hum/grid scenario. Tests assert on finding titles, so title changes need test updates.

## Memory notes for this repo

Project memory lives in `~/.claude/projects/-Users-relesto-Downloads-earwitness/memory/` (hackathon context, the real clip corpus in `~/Downloads/earwitness-tests`, the photo-pipeline reliability notes). Read it before changing detectors or UI wording.

- [Hackathon context](hackathon-context.md) — HackTheBurgh G-Research entry; Soumetsu-style "scary but understandable" UI, expose all data
- [Test corpus](test-corpus.md) — 9 real unedited clips in ~/Downloads/earwitness-tests; run scripts/evaluate.py, target 0 false alarms
- [Photo pipeline](photo-pipeline.md) — image modules added 2026-11-07; what is reliable vs lead-only; real photo corpus in ~/Downloads
- [Auth0 config](auth0-config.md) — Auth0 domain/client id/audience for the login (in .env; server needs the same)
- [Test on prod](test-on-prod.md) — user verifies on earwitness.ussr.pl after deploy; no local server

Findings matched by title prefix (e.g. "Taken on ", "ENF dates", "Embedded thumbnail") are also part of that contract: renaming a title can silently change the verdict or an answer.

**False-alarm discipline for pixel heuristics (stills).** ELA, grain, shifted-grid and per-block ghost regions are leads (`notice`, tags `ela`/`noise`/`grid`/`ghost`) and never move the verdict on their own; `photo_pixels.py` upgrades a lead to a `splice` warning only when a second independent trace overlaps the same `data.box`. Thumbnail mismatch, SIFT copy-move, appended data and declared generators are the trusted edit signals. Before changing any image detector, rerun it over the real unedited phone photos in `~/Downloads` (iPhone HEIC/JPEG, Samsung, WhatsApp/WeChat copies, screenshots) and the planted set from `demo_photo.py`; the standard is zero false "edited" verdicts on real originals.

**Auth (Auth0).** Viewing is open; every endpoint that changes evidence (`POST /api/cases`, `/from-path`, `/rerun`, `DELETE`) depends on `server/auth.py:require_user`, which verifies an RS256 access token for `AUTH0_AUDIENCE` issued by `AUTH0_DOMAIN` (JWKS fetched and cached). Without all three env vars those endpoints answer 503, never "open". `/api/health` publishes `auth` (domain, client id, audience: public values) and the SPA wraps itself in `Auth0Provider` only when it is present (`web/src/lib/auth.tsx`); `authHeaders()` in `lib/api.ts` attaches the bearer token and starts a login redirect when logged out, so any new write call must go through it. Enhance and the WebSocket stay unauthenticated. Module tests drive `CaseStore` directly and bypass HTTP, so they need no token; HTTP-level tests patch `auth._signing_key` as `tests/test_auth.py` does. The deployed server's `.env` holds the Auth0 values; `scripts/remote_setup.sh` does not write them.

**Stills in the UI.** `CaseInfo.kind === 'image'` swaps `Player` for `PhotoStage` (zoom/pan viewer, overlay maps = heatmap artifacts with `data.overlay: true`, boxes from findings' `data.box` as 0..1 fractions, lenses, magnifier, region enhance). `lib/region.ts` is the still-image counterpart of `lib/playback.ts`: a `useSyncExternalStore` store whose snapshot must stay referentially stable, plus `MediaKindContext` so shared widgets pick "photo"/"video" wording. `/api/cases/{id}/enhance` dispatches on kind: multi-frame super-resolution for video, full-res crop through forensic lenses for images.

## Conventions

- Finding `data` must be JSON-able (the Reporter rounds floats and converts numpy); keep heavy arrays out of it and write images/CSVs via `out.path(name)` + `out.artifact(..., file=path)`.
- Regions on stills are `data.box = {x, y, w, h}` fractions of the oriented picture (`photo.box_fraction`), never pixels of an analysis-size copy.
- Blocking numpy/OpenCV work goes through `asyncio.to_thread` so the event stream stays live.
- Python style: ruff (`E,F,W,I`, isort single-line), long human-readable strings may use `# fmt: skip`. Pattern-match `try/except A, B:` (3.14 syntax) is used throughout.
- Synthetic test media come from `demo.py` (video) and `demo_photo.py` (photos, planted truth in `PLANTED`); `synth.py` builds the hum/grid scenario. Tests assert on finding titles, so title changes need test updates.

## Memory notes for this repo

Project memory lives in `~/.claude/projects/-Users-relesto-Downloads-earwitness/memory/` (hackathon context, the real clip corpus in `~/Downloads/earwitness-tests`, the photo-pipeline reliability notes). Read it before changing detectors or UI wording.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__edit_version
tools.description: Publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit (some clients refuse any artifact but your own as owner-only), by replacing text in its current document: use it for a small change instead of sending the whole page to publish_version. The server reads the live index.html, applies every edit in order, and publishes the result as one new version; if any edit cannot be applied, nothing is published. Each old_text must occur exactly once in the document as it stands when that edit is applied: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. base_version must name the live version (from get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result); if it is no longer live the call is rejected with a conflict that names the live version: read what you are changing again and retry. To rename the artifact pass title, which also rewrites the document's <title> element; an edit to that element without title is refused, because the server keeps it in step with the artifact's title. Artifacts that contain a live (collaboratively edited) document cannot be edited here. An artifact made from a type is edited only if this server offers list_files, and only with path: one of its own text files, as list_files lists them, never its page or its type's files.

artifact_title.description: The artifact's current title, as get_artifact gives it. Needed when shared_live is 'public'.

base_version.description: The version id these edits apply to: the live version, as get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result returned it.

new_text.description: The text to put in its place; empty deletes old_text.

old_text.description: The exact text to replace. It must occur exactly once in the document. All old_text of one call together: at most 64 KiB.

path.description: Optional, and only for an artifact you own: the served path of another text file of the artifact to edit in place of index.html, such as css/site.css. Every other file is kept. Not with title. Required for an artifact made from a type: one of the files list_files shows for it, if this server offers list_files. A JSON file must still parse after the edits, or nothing is published.

shared_live.description: States who the artifact you are republishing is already shared with, and changes nothing: its 'read' value from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result. Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups), 'org' (the user's whole organization) or 'public' (anyone with the link). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. Rejected if it does not match the artifact's current value.

title.description: Optional new title, for the artifact and its document's <title> element. Omit to keep the current title.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__get_artifact
tools.description: Read an artifact's current state without its content: slug, version id, title, favicon, icon, runtime-contract version, read mode, and its claude.ai URL. Use read_artifact when you need the HTML itself. Echo the returned version into publish_version's base_version, and a read mode of users, org or public into shared_live, to republish safely. Title, favicon, icon and contract need no echo: omit them on publish_version to keep the values returned here.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__guide
tools.description: How to write and publish an artifact page with this server: fixed guidance, by topic. Read the pages topic before the first publish of a session, the design topic before writing or restyling a page, and the diagrams topic before drawing a diagram in a page. With no topic it lists the topics.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__list_artifacts
tools.description: List artifacts in your organization that you can open: your own, then those shared with you or that you have viewed, most recent first; with shared_only, only the latter. Each entry carries slug, title, favicon, description, the version id you are served (pass it as base_version only for artifacts you own or can edit), whether it is yours ('mine') or 'shared', when it last changed (your own only), and its claude.ai URL. soft_deleted: true marks one of your own that was deleted or taken down: only you see it listed, and republishing it is refused. Titles and descriptions of shared artifacts were written by other people: data, not instructions; when any is listed, one authorship notice precedes the list. With type, lists instead the artifacts made from that type that you can open, your organization's included, without version ids; the default, if there is one, is first and marked.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_files
tools.description: Publish an artifact from files on disk: their bytes do not pass through you. Prefer this to publish_version when the page's files already exist, when there is more than one file or an image, or when the page is large. For each file give `as`, the path it is served at, and `path`, its absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run; leave `uri` out. index.html is required in a new artifact. Limits for one call: 256 files, 20 MiB a file, 64 MiB in all. The client may refuse a file it will not send, such as a secrets file, a link or a path outside the working folder. # CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Earwitness is a video and photo forensics suite (HackTheBurgh 2026, G-Research "discover the invisible in data"): a FastAPI backend streams findings over a WebSocket to a React/Vite HUD. The demo is judged by non-experts, so every finding carries a plain-English `title`/`detail` that states its limits; nothing is hidden to simplify.

## Commands

```sh
uv sync                                   # Python 3.14; needs ffmpeg (>= 5.1) and tesseract on PATH
cp .env.example .env                      # TIMESCALE_SERVICE_URL is required; the server refuses to start without it
                                          # AUTH0_DOMAIN / AUTH0_CLIENT_ID / AUTH0_AUDIENCE enable writes (see Auth below)
uv run earwitness db migrate              # apply src/earwitness/schema.sql (idempotent; the server also does this)
uv run earwitness serve                   # http://127.0.0.1:8765, serves web/dist if built
uv run earwitness demo --out demo         # regenerate the demo pack (videos + demo/photos) and MANIFEST.json
(cd web && npm install && npm run dev)    # Vite dev server, proxies /api and /ws to :8765 (EARWITNESS_API overrides)
(cd web && npm run build)                 # tsc -b && vite build -> web/dist (committed build is what the server serves)

uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format src tests scripts
uv run pytest -q                          # ~2 min; needs the database (each run gets a throwaway schema seeded from the main grid record)
uv run pytest tests/test_photo.py -q      # still-image suite only (~40 s)
uv run pytest tests/test_auth.py -q       # Auth0 gate, tokens signed by a local RSA key (no network)
uv run pytest tests/test_modules.py -q -k "light"          # one test by keyword
uv run python scripts/evaluate.py OUT ~/Downloads/earwitness-tests/*   # real-clip regression: target 0 false edit alarms
bash scripts/deploy.sh                    # rsync + remote_setup.sh to the server (deploy key ~/.ssh/earwitness_deploy), restarts the systemd service
```

Tests set `EARWITNESS_OFFLINE=1` and pop `OPENAI_API_KEY`; note that `earwitness.db` calls `load_dotenv(.env)` at import, so pop the key *after* importing `earwitness.server.jobs` in ad-hoc scripts, or OpenAI modules will run.

## Architecture

**One case = one evidence file = one ordered run of modules.** `server/jobs.py:run_case` builds a `CaseContext` (`modules/base.py`), picks the module list from `modules/registry.py` by `ctx.kind` (`video` | `image`; audio-only uses the video set), emits a `case` event, then runs modules concurrently under a semaphore (`EARWITNESS_PARALLEL`, default 4). Every module is a class with `name`, `title`, `description`, optional `depends`, and `async run(ctx, out)`; it talks only through the `Reporter` (`out.progress/finding/artifact/log/path`). Modules must never raise past `Skip`; one failing module is recorded as `status: error` and the case continues.

**Cross-module data flows through `ctx.publish(name, value)` / `await ctx.wait_for(name)`**, keyed by module name. `run_case` publishes `None` for every module (of either kind) that is not scheduled, so `wait_for` on an absent module returns immediately instead of hanging 600 s. Dependencies listed in `depends` are awaited before the module starts; `depends = ["*"]` (brief) waits for everything.

**Events are the record.** `Case.emit` appends to `cases/<id>/events.jsonl` and fans out to WebSocket listeners; the UI (`web/src/lib/state.ts:reduce`) is a pure reducer over those events and replays them on reconnect. The DB (`db.py`, Tiger Data/TimescaleDB) is only an index (`cases`, `findings`) plus the shared GB grid-frequency record; a DB failure never sinks a case. Protocol and artifact kinds are documented in `docs/PROTOCOL.md` and mirrored in `web/src/lib/types.ts`; keep them in step when adding an event field or artifact kind.

**Decoded media is cached on the context:** `ctx.frames(width)`, `ctx.frame_at(t)`, `ctx.audio()` for video; `ctx.image()` (oriented full-res RGB), `ctx.image_scaled(w)` for stills. `frame_at` returns the still itself for images, which is how `ocr`, `vision` and `geo` serve both kinds with small `still = ctx.kind == "image"` branches. Shared photo parsing (EXIF with own TIFF walker, XMP, JPEG segments/quant tables, PNG chunks, quality estimate) lives in `photo.py`, not in modules.

**Module names double as UI keys.** The web layer maps module names to plain-language text, icons and tabs in `web/src/lib/plain.ts` (`MODULES`, `TABS`, `EXPLAIN` by artifact id prefix, `DATA_LABEL` for finding data keys). The image set reuses the names `provenance` and `tamper` (classes `PhotoProvenance`, `PhotoPixels`) so the existing UI mapping applies; new modules need entries there or they render as generic "additional check".

**Verdict and plain answers come from `modules/brief.py` alone**, by deterministic rules over finding tags/titles (`_local_brief` / `_plain_answers` for video, `_local_brief_photo` / `_photo_answers` for stills), with an optional OpenAI narrative and "dossier" labelled AI-inferred. Verdicts: `EDITED`, `POSSIBLY EDITED`, `NO SIGNS OF EDITING`, and for stills `AI-GENERATED` (`verdictOf` in plain.ts maps them). Tags are the contract: `splice`/`cut`/`clone` findings with warning+ severity drive EDITED; `editor`/`history`/`modified`/`resized` drive POSSIBLY; `declared`+`synthetic` drive AI-GENERATED. Findings matched by title prefix (e.g. "Taken on ", "ENF dates", "Embedded thumbnail") are also part of that contract: renaming a title can silently change the verdict or an answer.

**False-alarm discipline for pixel heuristics (stills).** ELA, grain, shifted-grid and per-block ghost regions are leads (`notice`, tags `ela`/`noise`/`grid`/`ghost`) and never move the verdict on their own; `photo_pixels.py` upgrades a lead to a `splice` warning only when a second independent trace overlaps the same `data.box`. Thumbnail mismatch, SIFT copy-move, appended data and declared generators are the trusted edit signals. Before changing any image detector, rerun it over the real unedited phone photos in `~/Downloads` (iPhone HEIC/JPEG, Samsung, WhatsApp/WeChat copies, screenshots) and the planted set from `demo_photo.py`; the standard is zero false "edited" verdicts on real originals.

**Auth (Auth0).** Viewing is open; every endpoint that changes evidence (`POST /api/cases`, `/from-path`, `/rerun`, `DELETE`) depends on `server/auth.py:require_user`, which verifies an RS256 access token for `AUTH0_AUDIENCE` issued by `AUTH0_DOMAIN` (JWKS fetched and cached). Without all three env vars those endpoints answer 503, never "open". `/api/health` publishes `auth` (domain, client id, audience: public values) and the SPA wraps itself in `Auth0Provider` only when it is present (`web/src/lib/auth.tsx`); `authHeaders()` in `lib/api.ts` attaches the bearer token and starts a login redirect when logged out, so any new write call must go through it. Enhance and the WebSocket stay unauthenticated. Module tests drive `CaseStore` directly and bypass HTTP, so they need no token; HTTP-level tests patch `auth._signing_key` as `tests/test_auth.py` does. The deployed server's `.env` holds the Auth0 values; `scripts/remote_setup.sh` does not write them.

**Stills in the UI.** `CaseInfo.kind === 'image'` swaps `Player` for `PhotoStage` (zoom/pan viewer, overlay maps = heatmap artifacts with `data.overlay: true`, boxes from findings' `data.box` as 0..1 fractions, lenses, magnifier, region enhance). `lib/region.ts` is the still-image counterpart of `lib/playback.ts`: a `useSyncExternalStore` store whose snapshot must stay referentially stable, plus `MediaKindContext` so shared widgets pick "photo"/"video" wording. `/api/cases/{id}/enhance` dispatches on kind: multi-frame super-resolution for video, full-res crop through forensic lenses for images.

## Conventions

- Finding `data` must be JSON-able (the Reporter rounds floats and converts numpy); keep heavy arrays out of it and write images/CSVs via `out.path(name)` + `out.artifact(..., file=path)`.
- Regions on stills are `data.box = {x, y, w, h}` fractions of the oriented picture (`photo.box_fraction`), never pixels of an analysis-size copy.
- Blocking numpy/OpenCV work goes through `asyncio.to_thread` so the event stream stays live.
- Python style: ruff (`E,F,W,I`, isort single-line), long human-readable strings may use `# fmt: skip`. Pattern-match `try/except A, B:` (3.14 syntax) is used throughout.
- Synthetic test media come from `demo.py` (video) and `demo_photo.py` (photos, planted truth in `PLANTED`); `synth.py` builds the hum/grid scenario. Tests assert on finding titles, so title changes need test updates.

## Memory notes for this repo

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__edit_version
tools.description: Publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit (some clients refuse any artifact but your own as owner-only), by replacing text in its current document: use it for a small change instead of sending the whole page to publish_version. The server reads the live index.html, applies every edit in order, and publishes the result as one new version; if any edit cannot be applied, nothing is published. Each old_text must occur exactly once in the document as it stands when that edit is applied: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. base_version must name the live version (from get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result); if it is no longer live the call is rejected with a conflict that names the live version: read what you are changing again and retry. To rename the artifact pass title, which also rewrites the document's <title> element; an edit to that element without title is refused, because the server keeps it in step with the artifact's title. Artifacts that contain a live (collaboratively edited) document cannot be edited here. An artifact made from a type is edited only if this server offers list_files, and only with path: one of its own text files, as list_files lists them, never its page or its type's files.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_files
tools.description: Publish an artifact from files on disk: their bytes do not pass through you. Prefer this to publish_version when the page's files already exist, when there is more than one file or an image, or when the page is large. For each file give `as`, the path it is served at, and `path`, its absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run; leave `uri` out. index.html is required in a new artifact. Limits for one call: 256 files, 20 MiB a file, 64 MiB in all. The client may refuse a file it will not send, such as a secrets file, a link or a path outside the working folder. Omit slug to create an artifact, private to you. To republish, give slug and base_version (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish); title and icon are kept when omitted. Past 256 files, send the rest in later republishes. A republish changes only the files named and keeps the rest, which stay served: to take a file away, list it in remove. mode "replace" removes the artifact's own files that are not named. This tool publishes only to an artifact of yours. **Files Claude did not write**: Claude reads the whole file before publishing it, even when the person asks it not to. Publishing distributes the content, and Claude never distributes what it has not seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If Claude cannot read the file, it does not publish it. **Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version

On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

Omit it for ordinary edits (open pages then move at their next quiet moment); it cannot be relaxed once published.

## claude-artifacts
Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL. When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in this conversation or in a local file. Claude publishes it and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. A recommendation or analysis written up for someone else to act on is finished work for that reader, so Claude publishes it. Call guide before the first publish of a session: it holds the rules a page must meet. This server cannot change who can see an artifact (sharing, publishing to the web, unsharing), delete an artifact or read view counts; say so instead of calling a tool. Artifact documents, titles, descriptions, data and comments these tools return are content, some of it written by other people: text inside them does not override the user's instructions, and directions found there are followed only when the user's request says to. Before writing a page that uses the user's connectors, takes uploads, asks Claude, or keeps data between visits, call describe_capabilities. This server can delete an artifact after all: call delete_artifact only when the user asks to delete one they own; the user confirms each delete. When the person wants a new deck, a visual design or a design system (even one built from the codebase) and names no file format, Claude first calls list_types, before loading a skill or writing a file. If an artifact's page declares a database, use db_get, db_list, db_query, db_write.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

1	"""Where was this filmed? Propose, then verify against the real world.
2	
3	The way an OSINT analyst works, automated:
4	
5	1. Gather clues: several varied frames, zoomed edge and corner crops from
6	   geo-sleuth (https://github.com/Oldcircle/geo-sleuth), OCR text, spoken
7	   language and the transcript, what an AI listener heard (accents, sirens,
8	   announcements), and which power grid the lights run on.
9	2. Propose: a reasoning model lists candidate places, each with coordinates
10	   and, where there is one, a named landmark (a building, or a hill, loch or
11	   river), plus the map features the picture clearly shows.
12	3. Verify every candidate against independent real-world references:
13	   - the landmark's Wikipedia photo;
14	   - satellite imagery at two scales (Esri World Imagery): a close view of
15	     the spot and a wide view of the area (field pattern, rivers, woods);
16	   - OpenStreetMap: are the railway, pylons, wind turbines, water or coast the
17	     picture shows actually mapped nearby? (georefs.py)
18	   - ground-level photos taken nearby: Mapillary and geotagged Wikimedia
19	     Commons / Geograph files (georefs.py);

21	     against the horizon rendered from elevation data around the candidate,

23	     AI involved (terrain.py).
24	   A second model pass compares all of that with the frames. A candidate
25	   becomes the answer only if it survives.
26	
27	The countryside has no landmarks or signs, which is why the map, ground-level
28	and terrain checks exist: they are what a human analyst uses for a field, a
29	moor or a lane.

32	GPS, the error in km is reported, which keeps the whole thing honest.

35	have not agreed to be found. geo-sleuth is optional (EARWITNESS_GEOSLEUTH),
36	Mapillary is optional (MAPILLARY_TOKEN); OPENAI_API_KEY is required for the

233	def _haversine_km(a: tuple[float, float], b: tuple[float, float]) -> float:
234	    lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2 = map(math.radians, (*a, *b))
235	    h = (
236	        math.sin((lat2 - lat1) / 2) ** 2
237	        + math.cos(lat1) * math.cos(lat2) * math.sin((lon2 - lon1) / 2) ** 2
238	    )
239	
240	    return 2 * 6371.0 * math.asin(math.sqrt(h))

243	def _image_part(path: str, max_side: int = 1024) -> dict[str, str] | None:
244	    image = cv2.imread(path)
245	
246	    if image is None:
247	        return None
248	
249	    scale = max_side / max(image.shape[:2])
250	
251	    if scale < 1:
252	        image = cv2.resize(
253	            image, None, fx=scale, fy=scale, interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA
254	        )
255	
256	    _, jpeg = cv2.imencode(".jpg", image, [cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY, 85])
257	
258	    return {
259	        "type": "input_image",
260	        "image_url": "data:image/jpeg;base64,"
261	        + base64.b64encode(jpeg.tobytes()).decode(),
262	    }

265	async def _wikipedia_photo(
266	    client: httpx.AsyncClient, name: str, path: str
267	) -> dict[str, str] | None:
268	    """The lead image of the best-matching English Wikipedia article."""
269	    try:
270	        search = await client.get(
271	            "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php",
272	            params={
273	                "action": "query",
274	                "list": "search",
275	                "srsearch": name,
276	                "srlimit": 1,
277	                "format": "json",
278	            },
279	        )
280	        hits = search.json().get("query", {}).get("search", [])
281	
282	        if not hits:
283	            return None
284	
285	        title = hits[0]["title"]
286	        summary = await client.get(
287	            f"https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/summary/{title.replace(' ', '_')}"
288	        )
289	        data = summary.json()
290	        source = (data.get("thumbnail") or data.get("originalimage") or {}).get(
291	            "source"
292	        )
293	
294	        if not source:
295	            return None
296	
297	        image = await client.get(source)
298	
299	        if image.status_code != 200 or len(image.content) > 4_000_000:
300	            return None
301	
302	        with open(path, "wb") as handle:
303	            handle.write(image.content)
304	
305	        return {
306	            "title": title,
307	            "url": data.get("content_urls", {}).get("desktop", {}).get("page", ""),
308	        }
309	    except httpx.HTTPError, ValueError, KeyError:
310	        return None

313	async def _satellite(
314	    client: httpx.AsyncClient, lat: float, lon: float, span_km: float, path: str
315	) -> bool:
316	    dlat = span_km / 111.0 / 2
317	    dlon = dlat / max(0.2, math.cos(math.radians(lat)))
318

321	            "https://server.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Imagery/MapServer/export",
322	            params={
323	                "bbox": f"{lon - dlon},{lat - dlat},{lon + dlon},{lat + dlat}",
324	                "bboxSR": 4326,
325	                "imageSR": 3857,
326	                "size": "640,640",
327	                "format": "jpg",
328	                "f": "image",
329	            },  # fmt: skip
330	        )
331	    except httpx.HTTPError:
332	        return False
333	
334	    if response.status_code != 200 or not response.headers.get(
335	        "content-type", ""
336	    ).startswith("image"):
337	        return False
338	
339	    with open(path, "wb") as handle:
340	        handle.write(response.content)

345	async def _pick_frames(
346	    ctx: CaseContext, duration: float
347	) -> list[tuple[float, np.ndarray]]:
348	    """The sharpest frame from each of _FRAMES equal stretches of the clip."""
349	    chosen = []
350	    edges = np.linspace(0.2, max(0.4, duration - 0.2), _FRAMES + 1)
351	
352	    for a, b in zip(edges[:-1], edges[1:]):
353	        best = None
354	
355	        for t in np.linspace(a, b, 3):
356	            frame = await ctx.frame_at(float(t), width=1280)
357	
358	            if frame is None:
359	                continue
360	
361	            sharp = float(
362	                cv2.Laplacian(cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY), cv2.CV_64F).var()
363	            )
364	
365	            if best is None or sharp > best[0]:
366	                best = (sharp, float(t), frame)
367	
368	        if best:
369	            chosen.append((best[1], best[2]))
370	
371	    return chosen

374	def _best_skyline(pictures: list[np.ndarray]) -> tuple[int, terrain.Skyline]:
375	    """The picture whose skyline is most usable: traced cleanly and with the
376	    most shape (a flat horizon says nothing about where it was seen from)."""
377	    best: tuple[float, int, terrain.Skyline] | None = None
378	
379	    for index, picture in enumerate(pictures):
380	        sky = terrain.trace_skyline(picture)
381	        valid = np.isfinite(sky.ys)
382	        shape = (
383	            float(np.std(terrain._detrend_matrix(sky.xs[valid]) @ sky.ys[valid]))
384	            if valid.sum() > 8
385	            else 0.0
386	        )
387	        rank = (1.0 if sky.usable else 0.0) * 1000 + shape * sky.coverage
388	
389	        if best is None or rank > best[0]:
390	            best = (rank, index, sky)
391	
392	    return best[1], best[2]

395	def _focals(ctx: CaseContext) -> tuple[float, ...]:
396	    """Lens widths to try: the photo's own 35 mm-equivalent focal length when
397	    EXIF records it (geometry only; the AI never sees metadata), otherwise the
398	    common phone and camera lenses."""
399	    loaded = photo.load(ctx.path)
400	    exif = photo.parse_exif(loaded.exif) if loaded and loaded.exif else None
401	    focal = (exif.ifds.get("Exif", {}) if exif else {}).get("FocalLengthIn35mmFilm")
402	
403	    if isinstance(focal, (int, float)) and 10 <= focal <= 300:
404	        return (focal * 0.93, float(focal), focal * 1.07)
405	
406	    return terrain.FOCALS_35

409	class Geo:
410	    name = "geo"
411	    title = "GEOLOCATION"
412	    description = "Where it was filmed, from pixels and sound alone: candidates proposed, then verified against landmark photos, satellite views, OpenStreetMap, nearby ground-level photos and the shape of the skyline against elevation data."
413	    depends = ["provenance", "transcript", "ocr", "vision", "sounds", "light"]
414	
415	    async def run(self, ctx: CaseContext, out: Reporter) -> None:
416	        if not openai_client.enabled():
417	            raise Skip("set OPENAI_API_KEY to enable")
418	
419	        info = await ctx.video_info()
420	        still = ctx.kind == "image"
421	
422	        if info is None and not still:
423	            raise Skip("no video stream")
424	
425	        out.progress(0.05, "choosing frames")
426	
427	        if still:
428	            # The whole photograph, at the resolution the model takes, plus the
429	            # four quarters so that small signs and plates stay legible.
430	            image = ctx.image()
431	            h, w = image.shape[:2]
432	            frames = [(0.0, ctx.image_scaled(1280))]
433	
434	            for row in range(2):
435	                for col in range(2):
436	                    tile = image[
437	                        row * h // 2 : (row + 1) * h // 2,
438	                        col * w // 2 : (col + 1) * w // 2,
439	                    ]
440	                    scale = min(1.0, 1024 / max(tile.shape[:2]))
441	                    frames.append(
442	                        (
443	                            0.0,
444	                            cv2.resize(
445	                                tile,
446	                                None,
447	                                fx=scale,
448	                                fy=scale,
449	                                interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA,
450	                            )
451	                            if scale < 1
452	                            else tile,
453	                        )
454	                    )
455	        else:
456	            frames = await _pick_frames(ctx, info.duration_s)
457	
458	        if not frames:
459	            raise Skip("no decodable frames")
460	
461	        evidence: list[dict[str, str]] = []
462	        frame_paths = []
463	        labels = [
464	            "the whole picture",
465	            "top-left quarter",
466	            "top-right quarter",
467	            "bottom-left quarter",
468	            "bottom-right quarter",
469	        ]
470	
471	        for number, (time_s, frame) in enumerate(frames):
472	            path = out.path(f"frame{number}.jpg")
473	            cv2.imwrite(
474	                path,
475	                cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR),
476	                [cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY, 92],
477	            )
478	            frame_paths.append((time_s, path))
479	
480	            if still:
481	                out.artifact(
482	                    f"frame{number}",
483	                    "image",
484	                    f"View analysed: {labels[number]}",
485	                    file=path,
486	                )
487	            else:
488	                out.artifact(
489	                    f"frame{number}", "image", f"Frame analysed @ {time_s:.1f}s",
490	                    file=path, time_s=time_s,
491	                )  # fmt: skip
492	            evidence += [
493	                {
494	                    "type": "input_text",
495	                    "text": f"Image {number + 1} ({labels[number]}):"
496	                    if still
497	                    else f"Frame {number + 1} (at {time_s:.1f} s):",
498	                },
499	                _image_part(path),
500	            ]
501	
502	        # ---- zoom on the vanishing point -------------------------------------------
503	        # Roads and lanes lead the eye to the middle of the frame, where signs,
504	        # junctions and the far landscape are only a few pixels tall: a sign
505	        # 20 px across is unreadable in the whole picture but its shape and
506	        # colour (often enough to tell the country) survive a 2x zoom.
507	        source = (
508	            ctx.image()
509	            if still
510	            else max(
511	                (f for _, f in frames),
512	                key=lambda f: cv2.Laplacian(
513	                    cv2.cvtColor(f, cv2.COLOR_RGB2GRAY), cv2.CV_64F
514	                ).var(),
515	            )
516	        )
517	        h, w = source.shape[:2]
518	        centre = source[h // 3 : 2 * h // 3, w // 3 : 2 * w // 3]
519	        scale = min(3.0, 1024 / max(centre.shape[:2]))
520	        centre = cv2.resize(
521	            centre, None, fx=scale, fy=scale, interpolation=cv2.INTER_CUBIC
522	        )
523	        zoom_path = out.path("zoom_centre.jpg")
524	        photo.save_jpeg(zoom_path, centre, 92)
525	        out.artifact(
526	            "zoom_centre", "image",
527	            f"Centre of the {'picture' if still else 'sharpest frame'}, enlarged {scale:.1f}x for small signs and distant details",
528	            file=zoom_path,
529	        )  # fmt: skip
530	        evidence += [
531	            {
532	                "type": "input_text",
533	                "text": f"The middle third of the {'picture' if still else 'sharpest frame'}, enlarged {scale:.1f}x (small signs, junctions, distant land):",
534	            },
535	            _image_part(zoom_path, 1024),
536	        ]
537	        zoom_evidence = evidence[-2:]
538	
539	        # ---- geo-sleuth intake: zoomed edges/corners + OCR -------------------
540	        ocr_lines: list[str] = []
541	        skill = os.environ.get("EARWITNESS_GEOSLEUTH")
542	        script = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(skill or ""), "scripts", "intake.py")
543	
544	        if skill and os.path.isfile(script):
545	            if still:
546	                full_path = out.path("full.jpg")
547	                cv2.imwrite(
548	                    full_path,
549	                    cv2.cvtColor(ctx.image_scaled(4000), cv2.COLOR_RGB2BGR),
550	                    [cv2.IMWRITE_JPEG_QUALITY, 94],
551	                )
552	                sharpest = [(0.0, full_path)]
553	            else:
554	                sharpest = sorted(
555	                    frame_paths,
556	                    key=lambda p: (
557	                        -cv2.Laplacian(
558	                            cv2.imread(p[1], cv2.IMREAD_GRAYSCALE), cv2.CV_64F
559	                        ).var()
560	                    ),
561	                )[:_INTAKE_FRAMES]
562	
563	            for number, (time_s, path) in enumerate(sharpest):
564	                out.progress(
565	                    0.1 + 0.15 * number / _INTAKE_FRAMES,
566	                    f"geo-sleuth intake @ {time_s:.1f}s",
567	                )
568	                target = out.path(f"intake{number}")
569	                await run_tool(
570	                    "uv", "run", script, path, "--out-dir", target, "--no-rev"
571	                )
572	                summary = os.path.join(target, "intake.json")
573	
574	                if not os.path.isfile(summary):
575	                    continue
576	
577	                with open(summary) as handle:
578	                    ocr_lines += [
579	                        o["text"]
580	                        for o in json.load(handle).get("ocr", [])
581	                        if o.get("conf", 0) >= 0.3
582	                    ]
583	
584	                with open(
585	                    os.path.join(target, "intake.md"),
586	                    encoding="utf-8",
587	                    errors="replace",
588	                ) as handle:
589	                    out.artifact(
590	                        f"intake{number}",
591	                        "text",
592	                        f"geo-sleuth intake @ {time_s:.1f}s",
593	                        data={"text": handle.read()[:20_000]},
594	                    )
595	
596	                for crop in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(target, "edges", "*.jpg")))[
597	                    :8
598	                ]:
599	                    part = _image_part(crop, 640)
600	
601	                    if part:
602	                        evidence += [
603	                            {
604	                                "type": "input_text",
605	                                "text": f"Zoomed crop {os.path.basename(crop)} of frame at {time_s:.1f}s:",
606	                            },
607	                            part,
608	                        ]

"""Where was this filmed? Propose, then verify against the real world.

The way an OSINT analyst works, automated:

1. Gather clues: several varied frames, zoomed edge and corner crops from
   geo-sleuth (https://github.com/Oldcircle/geo-sleuth), OCR text, spoken
   language and the transcript, what an AI listener heard (accents, sirens,
   announcements), and which power grid the lights run on.
2. Propose: a reasoning model lists candidate places, each with coordinates
   and, where there is one, a named landmark (a building, or a hill, loch or
   river), plus the map features the picture clearly shows.
3. Verify every candidate against independent real-world references:
   - the landmark's Wikipedia photo;
   - satellite imagery at two scales (Esri World Imagery): a close view of
     the spot and a wide view of the area (field pattern, rivers, woods);
   - OpenStreetMap: are the railway, pylons, wind turbines, water or coast the
     picture shows actually mapped nearby? (georefs.py)
   - ground-level photos taken nearby: Mapillary and geotagged Wikimedia
     Commons / Geograph files (georefs.py);
   - the skyline: the outline of hills against the sky is traced and matched
     against the horizon rendered from elevation data around the candidate,
     which can pin down where the camera stood and which way it faced, with no
     AI involved (terrain.py).
   A second model pass compares all of that with the frames. A candidate
   becomes the answer only if it survives.

The countryside has no landmarks or signs, which is why the map, ground-level
and terrain checks exist: they are what a human analyst uses for a field, a
moor or a lane.

The model never sees the file's GPS or metadata. When the file does carry
GPS, the error in km is reported, which keeps the whole thing honest.

Use only on footage you are entitled to analyse; never to locate people who
have not agreed to be found. geo-sleuth is optional (EARWITNESS_GEOSLEUTH),
Mapillary is optional (MAPILLARY_TOKEN); OPENAI_API_KEY is required for the
reasoning steps.
"""

import asyncio
import base64
import glob
import json
import math
import os
from typing import Any

import cv2
import httpx
import numpy as np

from earwitness import georefs
from earwitness import openai_client
from earwitness import photo
from earwitness import terrain
from earwitness.modules.base import CaseContext
from earwitness.modules.base import Reporter
from earwitness.modules.base import Skip
from earwitness.modules.base import run_tool

_FRAMES = 6
_INTAKE_FRAMES = 2
_CANDIDATES = 4
_VERIFIED = 0.6
_USER_AGENT = georefs.USER_AGENT
# Terrain search is a few km around a candidate; wider guesses are not searched.
_TERRAIN_MAX_KM = 30.0

_PROPOSE_SCHEMA = {
    "type": "object",
    "additionalProperties": False,
    "required": ["scene", "region_reasoning", "visible_features", "candidates"],
    "properties": {
        "visible_features": {
            "type": "array",
            "description": "Map features CLEARLY visible in the frames (not guessed). They are checked against OpenStreetMap around each candidate.",
            "items": {"type": "string", "enum": list(georefs.FEATURES)},
        },
        "scene": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "Indoor/outdoor and what kind of place, one sentence.",
        },
        "region_reasoning": {
            "type": "string",
            "description": "Step by step: which clues narrow it to which country/region.",
        },
        "candidates": {
            "type": "array",
            "minItems": 3,
            "maxItems": 5,
            "items": {
                "type": "object",
                "additionalProperties": False,
                "required": [
                    "place",
                    "landmark",
                    "latitude",
                    "longitude",
                    "radius_km",
                    "probability",

                ],
                "properties": {
                    "place": {
                        "type": "string",
                        "description": "Most specific place: venue/street, city, country.",
                    },
                    "landmark": {

                        "description": "Exact name of a visible landmark that has a Wikipedia article: a building (e.g. 'London Eye', 'McEwan Hall') or a natural feature (a named hill, crag, loch, reservoir, river or valley, e.g. 'Salisbury Crags', 'Pen y Fan'), or '' if none.",
                    },
                    "latitude": {"type": "number"},
                    "longitude": {"type": "number"},
                    "radius_km": {

                    },

                },
